item.content:encoded: A drone attack from Iraq forced Saudi Arabia to close its East-West pipeline, the kingdom said, threatening a key workaround to Iran’s Persian Gulf blockade.

item.title: Portsmouth experiences second weekend of anti-immigration protests
item.author: Sammy Gecsoyler and Raphael Boyd
item.content:encoded: Rightwing activists faced a heavy police presence and counter-demonstrations to their march against small boat crossingsTwo men and a teenage boy have been arrested in Portsmouth at a far-right protest against immigration.Far-right activists have gathered in Portsmouth for a second weekend after a small boat with 140 people seeking asylum on board was intercepted last Sunday while heading towards the city.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We Left in the Clothes We Were Wearing’: Yemenis Flee New Fighting
item.author: Saeed Al-Batati, Shuaib Almosawa and Somini Sengupta
item.content:encoded: Hunger and disease have tormented Yemen for years. Now, fighting between the Saudi-backed government and Iran-backed Houthis is pushing it to the brink.

item.title: Mississippi police say more arrests to come in death of woman found hanging from tree
item.author: Associated Press
item.content:encoded: Officials still investigating death of Tasia Fortune, a Black woman, a day after man’s arrest in relation to killingMississippi police said on Saturday they were still investigating the death of Tasia Fortune, a Black woman found hanging from a tree last month, a day after a man was arrested in connection with the killing.Loved ones also painted a picture of Fortune as a mother, athlete and woman of faith who they hoped would not solely be remembered for her horrific death.Continue reading...

item.title: Donations of £72m make Reform’s prospects both rosier and riskier
item.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
item.content:encoded: Party can boost its campaign power with funds from billionaire backers, but it can also lose support from ordinary BritonsAll things being equal, pretty much any political strategist would welcome a £72m war chest; a sum higher than the combined spending of every major party at the 2024 general election. But all things are not equal, and with such a huge amount comes risk.Reform UK has been vocal in its arguments that two sudden £36m windfalls from billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne merely “levels the playing field” with the bigger parties when it comes to funding.Continue reading...

item.title: Donald Trump says he would ‘love’ to see united Ireland
item.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
item.content:encoded: US president says on visit to republic that unification will happen eventually so ‘may as well happen now’Donald Trump has said he would “love” to see a united Ireland and that it “may as well happen now”.The US president appeared to endorse the push for constitutional change on the island at the start of a two-day visit to Ireland on Saturday. The unexpected intervention prompted a swift rebuttal from the UK government and Northern Ireland’s unionist leaders.Continue reading...

item.title: Number of UK anti-migrant vigilante groups surges in last 18 months
item.author: Patrick Greenfield and Michael Goodier
item.content:encoded: Exclusive: Many ‘use community protection as a cover for racist thuggery’, raising concerns about fresh disorderAt least 28 anti-migrant vigilante groups have formed in the UK in the last 18 months, ranging from unauthorised street patrols claiming to protect women and children to groups harassing migrants in France and blocking ports.From Belfast to the south coast of England, the number of active groups has surged since the summer of 2025, according to analysis by the Guardian, amid widespread concerns over fresh disorder after black-clad vigilantes, many of them wearing balaclavas, blocked roads in Portsmouth and Dover last weekend.Continue reading...

item.title: Why Tech Oligarchs Are Willing to Risk Apocalypse
item.author: Michelle Goldberg
item.content:encoded: Silicon Valley’s strange new theology.

item.title: ‘We must slow the pace’: CEO of Anthropic calls for an AI slowdown
item.author: Edward Helmore
item.content:encoded: In a social media post, Dario Amodei proposed a plan including third-party evaluations of AI systemsThe CEO of the artificial intelligence company Anthropic issued a new appeal on Saturday for the AI industry to “slow down” and offered a three-part plan for doing so, saying that his company would “unilaterally” commit to the first of the steps.In a post on social media, Dario Amodei shared a link to an essay titled We Must Pace the Frontier in which he lays out how Anthropic would provide “third-party evaluators with permanent, employee-level access to our systems, so that they can verify adherence to our safety measures, report on incidents, and assess models’ alignment during training”.Continue reading...

item.title: Saudi Arabia shuts down key oil pipeline, blaming drones from Iraq
item.author: Oliver Holmes and agencies
item.content:encoded: Riyadh has increased use of East-West pipeline since start of war on Iran to bypass closure of strait of HormuzSaudi Arabia has shut down a critical oil pipeline, accusing militants in Iraq of launching drone attacks on the export route being used to bypass the lockdown of the strait of Hormuz.The world’s largest ⁠crude oil exporter has increased its use of the 745-mile (1,200km) pipeline running across the Arabian peninsula, which links Abqaiq, near the Gulf, to the port of Yanbu, on the Red Sea, since the US-Israeli war against Iran began.Continue reading...

item.title: Christopher Harborne matches £36m Reform donation of Ben Delo
item.author: Geraldine McKelvie
item.content:encoded: Party leader, Nigel Farage, ‘humbled’ by contributions from billionaires as Harborne addresses ‘media speculation’The pledges mean Reform has received a cash injection of £72m in just 24 hours. They are jointly the largest donations made to a UK political party and have intensified calls for restrictions on money received from individual donors.Continue reading...

item.title: Burial of King Oyo takes place in Uganda as news anchor prepares for throne
item.author: Reuters in Kampala
item.content:encoded: Royal guards carry casket through streets of Fort Portal amid row over appointment of Edward Rukidi KijanangomaUganda’s King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, long the world’s youngest monarch, has been buried among the tombs of his royal forebears as ⁠his Tooro kingdom looked to put ⁠a bitter succession battle behind ​it.Oyo’s appointed successor, the news anchor Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, cast nine coffee berries into the grave at the Karambi Royal Tombs, marking the formal handover of power in the western Ugandan kingdom.Continue reading...

item.title: Taxes wouldn’t fund $5,000 Trump ‘dividend’ if Republicans win midterms, says commerce secretary
item.author: Edward Helmore
item.content:encoded: Lutnick said $500bn of estimated $1tn needed to fund checks to all US adults could come from new visa programDonald Trump’s controversial proposal to give a $5,000 “dividend” to all US adults if Republicans maintain control of Congress in November’s elections would not be paid out from US tax revenues, according to the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick.“It’s not tax money,” Lutnick said in an interview with NBC News, adding that the administration could “earn the money that Donald Trump wants to pay out, not from the deficit and not from taxpayers”.Continue reading...

item.title: Six Nigerians extradited to US over $6M online romance scam
item.author: Guardian staff and Associated Press
item.content:encoded: Alleged members of Black Axe criminal network that swindled US women out of $6m flown from South AfricaSix Nigerian nationals linked to an organized criminal network that allegedly swindled American women out of more than $6m through online romance scams were extradited to the United States on Friday.South African police confirmed they were to be extradited earlier on Friday, while local news in Africa confirmed that the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, known as the Hawks, facilitated their handover to officials from the US Federal Bureau of Investigation and Secret Service at Cape Town international airport, in collaboration with Interpol South Africa.Continue reading...

item.title: Jeremy Thomas, British producer of The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, dies aged 77
item.author: Andrew Pulver
item.content:encoded: An outstanding figure in the UK film industry, Thomas was noted for collaborations with directors including Bernardo Bertolucci and David CronenbergJeremy Thomas, the distinguished British producer of films including Sexy Beast, High-Rise and the multi-Oscar-winning The Last Emperor, has died aged 77.A representative for Thomas said he died on Friday “peacefully, at his country home in Oxfordshire, surrounded by his family and loved ones”.Continue reading...

item.title: IDF soldier filmed shooting Palestinian in leg amid West Bank settler standoff
item.author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
item.content:encoded: Incident is latest to raise questions over Israel’s ability or willingness to stop violent settlers in occupied territoryAn Israeli soldier has shot a Palestinian man, wounding him in the leg, as settlers confronted villagers by grazing livestock on Palestinian-owned land in the town of Faqqua in the occupied West Bank.Witnesses said a group of settlers had entered the area with their livestock, prompting residents to try to stop them. Israeli forces then intervened and, according to men at the scene, opened fire at residents. One of them shot Qassem Hussam, a Palestinian man in his mid-30s, wounding him in the leg.Continue reading...

item.title: Nashville airport board unanimously approves name change to honor Dolly Parton
item.author: Edward Helmore
item.content:encoded: The city’s mayor and Tennessee’s governor threw their support behind the name change last monthThe Nashville airport is to be renamed after Dolly Parton, a board of commissioners voted on Friday, in tribute to the Smoky Mountain singer who is estimated to bring $1.8bn each year to Tennessee through her Dollywood theme park.The decision ensures that Parton, who died last month at 80 years old, will be memorialized with her name on an airport, although the renaming process will take time to complete.Continue reading...

item.title: Why Mokha, Historic Port That Shaped the Coffee Trade, Is a Prize in Yemen’s War
item.author: Jonathan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: A strategic location on the Red Sea afforded the city centuries of trading dominance — and makes it a coveted target in today’s fighting in the Middle East.

item.title: Manhattan Bus Lane Plan for 34th Street May Be Stuck in Gridlock
item.author: Stefanos Chen
item.content:encoded: Months after Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the city would proceed with a redesign of 34th Street that had been halted by the Trump administration, the plan is no closer to completion.

item.title: Xi Jinping gets red carpet at Brics summit amid thaw in India-China relations
item.author: Oliver Holmes
item.content:encoded: Chinese president’s arrival in Delhi seen as step towards reconciliation after deadly 2020 military clashThe Chinese president, Xi Jinping, has received a red-carpet welcome in India for a summit of Brics developing nations, as regional rivals Beijing and Delhi make a public display of thawing relations while quietly competing to lead at a time of shaky US global dominance.As Xi stepped off the plane, he was walked past an honour guard of Indian soldiers and traditional dancers in colourful dresses. Later on Saturday, he was due to attend a gala dinner for the two-day summit.Continue reading...

item.title: Calls for Democrats to be shot go unchallenged at Republican convention
item.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
item.content:encoded: Crowd member repeatedly said some Democrats ‘should be shot’ during Ted Cruz’s speech, without senator respondingOn the night Republicans gathered to mourn the killing of Charlie Kirk and warn against the dangers of violent rhetoric, a crowd at the party’s irregular midterm convention in Dallas repeatedly called for a sitting Senate candidate to be shot, while the Republican senator at the podium never denounced or even noted the outbursts.The outbursts came repeatedly during Ted Cruz’s Thursday night address at the American Airlines center, when he named a Democrat he accused of holding radical views. After the senator mentioned the New York City mayor, Zohran Mamdani, video footage depicts at least one audience member shouting: “He should be shot!” The same cry followed when Cruz named Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, and again after he named Texas Senate candidate James Talarico. Cruz did not pause or respond to the shouting, and it remains unclear whether he heard it from the stage. Cruz did not respond to a request for comment.Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: The $5,000 election promise shows how afraid Trump really is.

item.author: Ana Ionova and Edward Wong
item.content:encoded: Officials say the Trump administration is blocking some of Brazil’s efforts to expand cooperation on fighting transnational crime.

item.title: Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor Say the End of the World Is Now on the Table
item.author: David Marchese
item.content:encoded: In a new book, the writers argue that a powerful coalition of “end times fascists” is just fine with the earth’s demise.

item.title: Sweden’s extremely close election could see far right enter government
item.author: Miranda Bryant Nordic correspondent
item.content:encoded: Latest poll shows 0.3-point gap between left and right blocs, with country’s reputation as global champion of human rights said to be at stakeSweden goes to the polls on Sunday in an extremely close election that could see the far right enter government for the first time if the country’s rightwing parties can form a majority.Opinion polls show the centre-left opposition alliance ahead, with Magdalena ⁠Andersson of the Social Democrats the favourite to become prime minister again after four years in opposition, but her bloc’s lead has narrowed considerably in the final days of the campaign.Continue reading...

item.title: Death toll from Philippines ferry fire rises to 35, as officials warn toll will grow
item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.content:encoded: The deadly fire had begun in the ferry’s cargo hold, then tore through the ship within secondsThe bodies of passengers killed in a ferry fire off the Philippines arrived at a port near the resort town of Coron, Palawan, on Saturday morning, as the country’s coast guard warned the death toll of 35 would grow.Tents were being set up to receive 30 bodies brought from the M/V June Aster, which ran aground near the tourist hotspot after a fire erupted on Wednesday evening and tore through the vessel “in seconds”.Continue reading...

item.title: Iran’s Houthi allies capture strategic island on vital oil shipping route
item.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
item.content:encoded: Rampant Yemeni fighters take control of island in narrow point of Bab al-Mandab strait, which Saudi is relying on for oil exportsYemen’s rampant Houthi forces have captured the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandab strait, expanding their control of the narrow waterway, one of the ​world’s vital shipping routes.The Iran-aligned Houthis took control of the volcanic island after forces allied to the UN-backed, Aden-based government left in the latest of a dramatic series of reverses along Yemen’s west coast in recent days, including the loss of the port city of Mocha on Thursday.Continue reading...

item.title: Alleged drone operator charged with murder after mistaken identity shooting in Sydney
item.author: Henry Belot
item.content:encoded: NSW police say 18-year-old was operating drone when arrested and likely ‘conducting surveillance on someone or some premises’A Sydney teenager has been charged with murder after police accused him of operating a drone as part of a suspected botched gang hit in the city’s west.Joshua Macdonald, 40, was shot dead at a Merrylands West home on 2 September in what police believe may have been a case of mistaken identity. He was not known to police and had no links to organised crime.Continue reading...

item.title: Nearly 50,000 Yemeni civilians flee as Houthis advance along Red Sea coast
item.author: Oliver Holmes
item.content:encoded: Global struggle for control of Bab al-Mandab strait threatens to turn Yemen’s on-off conflict into a forever warCivilians in the Middle East’s poorest country have found themselves victims of a global struggle for control over one of the most important shipping routes in the world, which threatens to turn Yemen’s on-off conflict into a forever war.Continue reading...

item.title: Firewall compromised: has Friedrich Merz blown ‘democracy’s last shot’?
item.author: Deborah Cole in Berlin
item.content:encoded: Many fear chancellor is wrong man for the job at a time when Germany’s defences against far right are crumblingA cataclysm. A 9.0 earthquake. A five-alarm fire. A bitter rejection of Germany’s joyous reunification three decades ago, and a threat to the democratic postwar order.Sizing up the repercussions of last weekend’s win for the far-right Alternative für Deutschland party in the former communist state of Saxony-Anhalt, German commentators expressed a sense of doom, panic and helplessness in the political establishment.Continue reading...

item.title: Court case brought by Zionist federation against journalist Mary Kostakidis ended ‘by consent’
item.author: Lisa Cox
item.content:encoded: Former SBS newsreader had been accused by Zionist Federation of Australia of breaching Racial Discrimination Act when sharing X postsFederal court proceedings brought by the Zionist Federation of Australia (ZFA) against journalist Mary Kostakidis have been discontinued “by consent” with “no order as to costs”.The former SBS newsreader had been accused by the federation of breaching the Racial Discrimination Act (RDA) by sharing two X posts about a speech by the late Hezbollah secretary general Hassan Nasrallah in January 2024.Continue reading...

item.title: NSW police seize 36 illegal ebikes on northern beaches that are now destined for the crusher
item.author: Henry Belot
item.content:encoded: Officers found one 14-year-old’s ebike was capable of hitting 90km/h. Owners have two weeks to appeal the seizure before the bikes will be crushedDozens of high-powered and illegal ebikes have been seized by police on Sydney’s northern beaches just weeks after the force was granted new powers to destroy dangerous bikes.The operation was part of a coordinated push with the New South Wales government to ensure people only ride legal ebikes that have not been modified to reach high speeds.Continue reading...

item.title: As China rises, Australia is increasingly enmeshed in the US war machine. Is the alliance still worth the risk?
item.author: Ben Doherty
item.content:encoded: Australia is being exploited by an ally that could draw it, however unwillingly, into war with China, experts warn“Physical security matters,” said Kevin Rudd, at his axiomatic best before the National Press Club this week.“Our first responsibility is to secure our people’s future in this most contested region of the world.”Continue reading...

item.title: CIA releases dozens of presidential daily briefs on Bin Laden and al-Qaida from before 9/11
item.author: Associated Press
item.content:encoded: The presidential briefing documents were declassified on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacksSeveral dozen presidential briefing documents declassified on Friday, the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, detail intelligence that government officials had gathered about Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida leading up to the hijackings that killed nearly 3,000 people and upended American national security.The documents illustrate security analysts’ tracking of Bin Laden’s movements and support system, as well as concerns about possible threats to US targets. They also detail officials’ understanding of his network in the United States and other countries, including how his operations were financed.Continue reading...

item.title: Trump and Hegseth use 9/11 memorial remarks at Pentagon to defend war on Iran
item.author: Shrai Popat and Joseph Gedeon in Washington
item.content:encoded: President and defense secretary try to link worst terrorist attack in US history to current unpopular warDonald Trump and Pete Hegseth used remarks at the memorial ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of 9/11 to defend the US-Israel war on Iran – and suggest the controversial conflict was part of the legacy of the worst terrorist attack in US history.While such ceremonies on September 11 typically focus on the victims of the 2001 attacks, the US president and his defense secretary each pointed to the war they launched on Iran more than six months ago, with no end in sight.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Absurd, hardline calls’: questions over Sweden’s post-Brexit migration policy
item.author: Lisa O’Carroll in Stockholm
item.content:encoded: Sweden has ordered more Britons, including vulnerable people, to leave post-Brexit than any other EU countryHe arrived with nothing other than the clothes he wore that morning. Hours later he was banged up in a detention centre close to a Stockholm airport to await deportation.Charles, a former business director from Cambridge, who did not want his full name published, moved to Sweden in 2017 to be with his Swedish wife, Lily, and applied to remain after Brexit, before the deadline of December 2021.Continue reading...

item.title: Buddhist monk arrested in Thailand on suspicion of embezzling $2.8m
item.author: Agence France-Press in Bangkok
item.content:encoded: Phra Wachirayan Wi arrested alongside woman he was filmed having sex with in latest scandal to hit country’s clergyPolice in Thailand have arrested a senior Buddhist monk on suspicion of embezzling $2.8m intended for his monastery, alongside a suspected female accomplice he was filmed having sex with.The case is the latest scandal to hit the clergy in the Buddhist-majority country, after a sex and extortion case involving senior monks last year prompted public outrage and calls for greater scrutiny of temple finances.Continue reading...

item.title: Dementia patients warned off seeking home care in case Australia’s aged care algorithm cuts funding
item.author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
item.content:encoded: FoI documents show senior health officials were warned of concerns about assessment tool weeks after it launchedPeople with dementia were warned not to apply for home support because of fears their care would be downgraded by the government’s aged care algorithm.Documents released to Guardian Australia under freedom of information (FoI) laws reveal the warnings came within weeks of the November rollout of the algorithm, which is used to determine funding packages and priority of need for older Australians requiring home support.Continue reading...

item.title: $15m fund launched to create ‘unstoppable momentum’ to end FGM worldwide
item.author: Karen McVeigh
item.content:encoded: Her Horizon Fund seeks $100m to stop practice harming 230m women and girls globally Frontline activists and leaders in the fight against female genital mutilation, which has affected more than 230 million women and girls worldwide, have welcomed an unprecedented $15.5m (£11.4m) fund aimed at creating “unstoppable momentum” to finally end the practice.The launch of the fund comes as women’s rights are increasingly under attack and donor funding is in sharp decline, particularly for work led by FGM survivors in local communities. It is thought to be the largest single philanthropic contribution to ending the practice of FGM.Continue reading...

item.title: Canada offers air defense support for Ukraine as Zelenskyy visits
item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.content:encoded: Canadian PM Mark Carney hosts president in Calgary, where he grew up alongside large Ukrainian communityCanada offered support on Thursday to boost Ukraine’s air defenses and help replenish its drone stocks, as the countries pledged to deepen their alliance during a visit by Volodymyr Zelenskyy.Mark Carney hosted the president of Ukraine in Calgary in the western province of Alberta, where the Canadian prime minister grew up among a large community of people with Ukrainian heritage.Continue reading...

item.title: Secret son revelation ignites bitter succession dispute in Ugandan kingdom
item.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
item.content:encoded: Family of late King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV reject committee’s choice of cousin and TV presenter as new monarchA traditional Ugandan kingdom has become engulfed in a bitter succession dispute after the family of a king who recently died rejected the selection of a television news anchor as his successor.King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who became the world’s youngest reigning monarch when he took the throne in the kingdom of Tooro in 1995 at the age of three, died on 27 August in the US, where he was receiving cancer treatment.Continue reading...

item.title: Japan seeks change to new UN world map over Russia 'misconception'
item.author: Agence France-Presse in Tokyo
item.content:encoded: The new ‘true-scale’ map shrinks Europe and North America while enlarging Africa – and depicts the disputed Kuril islands as ruled by MoscowJapan has asked for the revision of a new world map adopted by the UN because it said it made the disputed Kuril islands appear to belong to Russia.The UN general assembly voted on Friday to adopt the new map, which makes the African continent larger while also shrinking North America and Europe, drawing condemnation from the US.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Our forefathers are coming back’: Naga people celebrate after Oxford museum agrees to return remains
item.author: Tora Agarwala
item.content:encoded: Following six years of talks, Pitt Rivers Museum will return body parts collected by British colonial administrators to north-east IndiaAnthropologists and community leaders from Nagaland, a remote state in north-eastern India bordering Myanmar, have expressed joy and relief that human remains belonging to their ancestors that had been on display in a British museum for nearly a century are finally being returned.On Monday, the Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford announced that 39 pieces of human remains – including parts of skulls, a finger and a piece of skin with hair – belonging to the Naga tribes, will be returned to Nagaland after six years of negotiation between the community and the museum.Continue reading...

item.title: Wall Street Journal publisher convicted in Hong Kong of deterring reporter from union role
item.author: Danny Vincent in Hong Kong
item.content:encoded: Dow Jones convicted of one count of deterring Selina Cheng from role at Hong Kong Journalist Association but cleared of second chargeA Hong Kong court has convicted the publisher of the Wall Street Journal of deterring a reporter from taking up a trade union role, in a case that raised concerns about press freedom in the city.The newspaper dismissed Selina Cheng just weeks after she was appointed chair of the Hong Kong Journalist Association (HKJA) in 2024. She was told at the time her termination was officially due to restructuring.Continue reading...

item.title: Rubio signals shift to working with allies to fight drug trade as latest boat strike kills three
item.author: Associated Press
item.content:encoded: Rubio visits Ecuador and welcomes cooperation after campaign of unilateral strikes on alleged ‘narco-terrorists’The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, gave new clarity on the approach toward combating drug trafficking in Latin American waters, saying the Trump administration was focused on working with allied countries and aligning with their laws but insisted the military would “still blow up ships if need be”.The public acknowledgment of a shift in US strategy comes a year after Washington began a campaign of unilateral deadly strikes against those it calls “narco-terrorists” operating boats in international waters.Continue reading...

item.title: Notorious Ecuadorian crime gang designated a terrorist group by US
item.author: Andrew Roth and agencies
item.content:encoded: Trump administration to seek extra funding from Congress to ‘dismantle’ Los Tiguerones over narcotics traffickingThe US has designated Ecuador’s Los Tiguerones gang, which stormed a television station during a live broadcast in 2024, as a terrorist organisation as the Trump administration expands its campaign against narcotics traffickers it says are destabilising Latin America.The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, made the announcement in Quito, where he met Ecuadorian president Daniel Noboa, one of several rightwing allies of Donald Trump whom Rubio is courting as a security partner during a three-nation tour through Latin America that began on Tuesday.Continue reading...
